title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. Choose one day to buy and a later day to sell to maximize profit. Return the maximum profit achievable, or 0 if no profit is possible.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price 1) and sell on day 5 (price 6) for profit 5.
Prices only fall, so no profitable trade exists.

hints: Track the minimum price seen so far while scanning left to right.
At each day, the best profit ending today is prices[i] - minPriceSoFar.
Keep the maximum of those daily profits across the whole scan.

solutions.title: All Pairs Check
One-Pass Min Tracking

editorial.approach: The brute-force check examines every pair of buying and selling days in O(n^2) time. The optimal approach maintains the minimum price seen so far in a single left-to-right pass. At each day i, calculate the potential profit prices[i] - min_price and update the global maximum profit.
editorial.why_optimal: A single pass achieves O(n) time and O(1) space, reducing quadratic comparisons down to a single streaming scan with zero extra heap allocations.
editorial.pitfalls: Resetting the minimum price without tracking the maximum profit achieved prior to that drop. Allowing selling before buying (e.g. taking max(prices) - min(prices) regardless of index ordering). Returning negative profit when prices strictly decrease instead of 0.
